title: BENCHLAB wire-protocol contract
description: Describes one (ProductId, FwVersion) pair's wire format. Generated from the firmware headers by tools/extract_protocol.py, which compiles a C probe using sizeof/offsetof under -fshort-enums -- the firmware is authoritative and no hand-maintained copy can drift from it. Downstream tooling should resolve a probed device to a contract via protocol/index.json and decode by the recorded offsets, never by hardcoded sizes.

status.description: released = devices are in the field with this firmware. Released contracts are immutable: extract_protocol.py refuses to overwrite one whose content would change, and the release workflow flips draft -> released as part of shipping.

variant.description: Contract-side product name. Note the firmware build targets are spelled benchlab1/benchlab2; this is the contract vocabulary and is what artifact names use.

identity.description: What the device reports from READ_VENDOR_DATA (0x0E). The (product_id, fw_version) pair is the key downstream gates on.

usb.description: Stock STMicroelectronics descriptors, identical on both products. Enumeration alone identifies neither a BENCHLAB nor its generation.

constants.description: #define values from the shared header and the variant config, e.g. SENSOR_POWER_NUM, TS_NUM, FIRMWARE_VERSION.

enum_width_bytes.description: Measured width of each protocol enum. Every one is 1 under -fshort-enums (the arm-none-eabi default), but the value is measured rather than assumed.

structs.description: Struct name -> layout. Sizes and offsets are what the compiler reported, with natural alignment and no packing.

type.description: A C scalar (uint8_t, int16_t, ...), an enum name from `enums`, or a nested struct name from `structs`.

array.description: null for a scalar field; otherwise the C array-dimension expression, which is a key in `constants` (e.g. "TS_NUM", "SENSOR_POWER_NUM"). Element count is size divided by the element width; the constant names which value governs it.

validation.description: Preconditions the firmware enforces; "none" when it accepts the bare opcode.

response.description: Struct name or symbolic payload name; null when the command sends nothing back.

response_size.description: Expected reply length in bytes; null when there is no reply. The protocol has no framing or length prefix, so this is the host's primary defence.

wire.description: Transport-level facts. The protocol is not self-describing: no framing, no length prefix, no checksum, no error responses.
